# Lab 5 — CI/CD & GitOps

## Task 1 — CI Pipeline and ArgoCD Setup

### 5.1 CI workflow

The repository contains a GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The workflow runs on pushes to `main`, builds Docker images for the Gateway, Events, and Payments services, logs in to GitHub Container Registry, and pushes the images to `ghcr.io` using the commit SHA as the image tag.

### 5.3 Kubernetes manifests updated for registry images

The Kubernetes manifests were updated to use images from GitHub Container Registry instead of local k3d images. The application images use `ghcr.io/rmcavalcante7/quickticket-*` references, `imagePullPolicy: Always`, and the `ghcr-secret` image pull secret so Kubernetes can pull the images from GHCR.

### 5.6 GitOps loop verification

A visible change was committed to Git by adding the label `version: "v2"` to the Gateway Pod template labels in `k8s/gateway.yaml`. After pushing the change and synchronizing ArgoCD, the label was visible in the live Kubernetes Deployment.

Command:

```bash
kubectl get deployment gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.metadata.labels.version}'; echo
```

Output:

```text
v2
```

Evidence of the synchronized label:

<img alt="kubectl output showing gateway Deployment template label version v2" src="data:image/png;base64,
" />

### 5.7 Proof of Work answer

If someone manually runs `kubectl edit` on a Kubernetes resource managed by ArgoCD, the live cluster state can become different from the desired state stored in Git. ArgoCD detects this difference as drift and marks the application or resource as `OutOfSync`.

The manual edit should not be treated as the source of truth. The desired state remains the manifest version stored in Git. When ArgoCD synchronizes the application, it reconciles the resource back to the Git-defined state. If automatic self-healing is enabled, ArgoCD can revert the manual change automatically; otherwise, the drift remains visible until a sync operation reconciles it.

## Task 2 — Rollback via GitOps

### 5.8 Bad deployment

A broken Gateway image tag was deployed through Git to test how the GitOps workflow handles a failed release. The manifest was changed to point the Gateway Deployment at a non-existent image tag, then the change was committed and pushed to `main`.

Command sequence:

```bash
git add k8s/gateway.yaml
git commit -m "ci: deploy bad gateway image"
git push origin main
```

After ArgoCD synchronized the commit, the QuickTicket application became degraded. The Gateway Deployment was the affected resource, while the other services stayed healthy.

Observed ArgoCD state:

```text
Sync Status:   Synced to (fb43e2b)
Health Status: Degraded
apps Deployment default gateway Synced Degraded deployment.apps/gateway configured
```

Observed Kubernetes state:

```text
gateway-564fdfd7db-m8jpr   0/1   ImagePullBackOff   0   25m
gateway-57dbd896bc-2wmll   1/1   Running            0   120m
```

This shows that the new Gateway Pod could not pull the requested image, while the previous healthy Gateway Pod continued serving during the failed rolling update.

Evidence:

<img alt="ArgoCD degraded after bad Gateway image and kubectl showing ImagePullBackOff" src="data:image/png;base64," />


### 5.9 Rollback through Git

The rollback was performed with `git revert`, so Git remained the source of truth and ArgoCD reconciled the cluster back to the previous healthy manifest.

Command sequence:

```bash
git revert HEAD --no-edit
git push origin main
```

Git history after the rollback:

```text
23f8040 Revert "ci: deploy bad gateway image"
1407e1e ci: deploy bad gateway image
0ea6d58 ci: update image tags to b3cccb06cc218ba2172aecfe5035df31f952f9c4
```

Evidence of the rollback commits:

<img alt="git log showing bad deployment commit followed by revert commit" src="data:image/png;base64," />


After the revert was pushed and synchronized, ArgoCD returned the application to a healthy state. The bad Gateway Pod was terminated and the healthy Gateway Pod remained running.

Observed ArgoCD state after rollback:

```text
Sync Status:   Synced to (23f8040)
Health Status: Healthy
apps Deployment default gateway Synced Healthy deployment.apps/gateway configured
```

Observed Kubernetes state after rollback:

```text
gateway-799954cc4b-z7md5   1/1   Running   0   30m
```

The recovery time from `git revert` and push to the healthy ArgoCD state was approximately 34 seconds. The revert commit was created at 17:33:07 UTC, and the ArgoCD view showed the application healthy at 17:33:41 UTC.

Evidence:

<img alt="ArgoCD healthy after git revert rollback and gateway pod running" src="data:image/png;base64," />


## Bonus Task — Automated Image Tag Update

The CI workflow was extended so that after building and pushing the service images, it updates the image tags in the Kubernetes manifests and commits those manifest changes back to `main`.

The workflow step updates all three service manifests:

```yaml
- name: Update image tags in manifests
  run: |
    SHA=${{ github.sha }}
    sed -i "s|image: ghcr.io/.*/quickticket-gateway:.*|image: ghcr.io/${{ github.actor }}/quickticket-gateway:${SHA}|" k8s/gateway.yaml
    sed -i "s|image: ghcr.io/.*/quickticket-events:.*|image: ghcr.io/${{ github.actor }}/quickticket-events:${SHA}|" k8s/events.yaml
    sed -i "s|image: ghcr.io/.*/quickticket-payments:.*|image: ghcr.io/${{ github.actor }}/quickticket-payments:${SHA}|" k8s/payments.yaml
```

The workflow also commits and pushes the updated manifests:

```yaml
- name: Commit and push manifest update
  run: |
    git config user.name "github-actions"
    git config user.email "github-actions@github.com"
    git add k8s/
    git diff --cached --quiet || git commit -m "ci: update image tags to ${{ github.sha }}"
    git push
```

To prevent an infinite loop, the workflow skips commits whose message starts with `ci:`:

```yaml
if: "!startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'ci:')"
```

A normal commit triggered the workflow, and GitHub Actions then created the automatic image-tag update commit.

Observed Git history:

```text
13aff17 ci: update image tags to 67e64cd2f3ed77837669aa34526cb1340a05c14e
67e64cd feat: add lab5 bonus workflow evidence
395b6e1 ci: update image tags to 23f8040b362daf9133d0abdc511a3b0dc12ad241
23f8040 Revert "ci: deploy bad gateway image"
1407e1e ci: deploy bad gateway image
```

After pulling the automatic commit, the manifests for Gateway, Events, and Payments were updated by CI. ArgoCD synchronized commit `13aff17` and deployed the new image tags. The application finished in `Synced` and `Healthy` state, with the three application Pods running successfully.

Observed ArgoCD state:

```text
Sync Status:   Synced to (13aff17)
Health Status: Healthy
```

Observed Kubernetes state:

```text
events-76f7cfbf6d-dfbzk     1/1   Running
gateway-64d4c65967-nv2tb    1/1   Running
payments-5fd99f8855-8jch9   1/1   Running
postgres-78489d7f5f-5vq96   1/1   Running
redis-6fcfb5475d-c95zn      1/1   Running
```
